name: Mine-to-mill reconciliation
summary: Every month the mine compares what it planned to mine, what the survey says was mined, what the tallies say was hoisted and trucked, and what the mill says it processed, in tonnes, grade and ounces, and explains the differences. A planning engineer compiles the tonnes from skip counts, truck loads, survey volumes and an estimate of broken ore still in the stopes, a mine geologist adds the grade control and reserve model grades, the metallurgist checks the mill numbers, and the chief geologist investigates gaps and writes the report for the technical services manager. The work is slow because the numbers sit in separate spreadsheets and survey files, much of the broken ore stays in open stopes between months, and tally or sampling errors only show up when the totals do not tie.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-650 tpd narrow-vein underground mine in northern Ontario, with a technical services department of about 20 engineers, surveyors and geologists on a 14-on, 14-off rotation.
baseline.notes: Practice follows the Eagle River mine technical reports (2016, 2022) and the neighbouring Island Gold report (2020); software is AutoCAD with Promine, Microsoft Access drillhole database, Excel workbooks and email, with Deswik and Leapfrog arriving in 2021.

trigger: The mill issues its month-end metallurgical balance (tonnes milled, calculated head grade and ounces recovered).
end_state: The reconciliation report with planned, mined, hoisted and milled tonnes, grade and ounces, the reconciliation factors and explained variances is issued to planning, site cost reporting and the reserve team.

volume.seasonality: One a month; the December reconciliation is extended into the year-end comparison with the reserve model.

evidence.note: Monthly comparison of production with the reserve model (island); periodic mine reconciliation led by geology (potvin).
9 mine engineering staff (er2022 Table 16-10); FTE share is the author's estimate from step times.
Geology monitors tonnes and grade of stopes and reconciles them with the mill (potvin); not listed among the process roles in the organisation file.
The periodic reconciliation is generally led by the geology department (potvin).
Checks mill-side tonnes, head grade and gold in circuit; author's estimate.
Reviews and issues the report; author's estimate.
Confirms tallies and misrouted loads; not listed among the process roles in the organisation file.

systems.name: Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Total stations, cavity monitoring scanner and survey software
Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)
Mill distributed control system and process historian
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)

steps.name: Receive the met balance and month-end inputs
steps.description: The planning engineer saves the mill's month-end metallurgical balance and collects the month's shift reports, haulage tallies, hoist log, stockpile survey and survey volumes into the reconciliation folder. Missing items are chased by email.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Compile hoisted, trucked and milled tonnes
steps.description: The engineer adds up skips hoisted at the certified 4 t payload, underground truck loads, surface truck loads from the portal pad to the mill 16.6 km away, and the mill weightometer tonnes, by day and source. Each count comes from a different sheet with its own load factor.

error.defect_description: A shift sheet is missed or counted twice, or a load factor is out of date.

evidence.note: Skip payload, underground trucks, portal pad rehandle and 16.6 km surface haul to the mill (er2022). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Load month-end survey volumes and stockpile surveys
steps.description: The engineer imports the surveyors' month-end development pick-ups, cavity monitoring scans of finished stopes and the portal pad and mill pad stockpile volumes. The step waits until survey has processed all month-end pick-ups.

evidence.note: Stope reconciliation starts with the cavity monitoring survey (potvin); CMS surveys are routine at the reference mine (er2022).

steps.name: Calculate mined tonnes from survey
steps.description: The engineer converts development metres and profiles and finished-stope cavity volumes into tonnes at 2.7 t/m3, split into ore and waste and by stope and heading.

error.defect_description: Wrong profile or a stope void counted in two months.

evidence.note: Bulk density of 2.7 t/m3 applied at the reference mine (er2022).

steps.name: Estimate broken ore left in open stopes
steps.description: Because LHDs only pull enough ore after each blast to make room for the next, most broken ore stays in the stope until the last blast. The engineer estimates the blasted tonnes from the ring designs and subtracts the mucked tally to get broken stock carried into next month.

error.defect_description: Broken stock estimate is off, shifting tonnes and ounces between months.

evidence.note: Shrink mucking leaves the majority of broken ore in the stope until blasting is complete (er2022).

steps.name: Compile grade control grades for tonnes mined
steps.description: The mine geologist assigns each heading's chip-composite grade, the muck sample grades and each stope's design grade to the tonnes mucked from it, giving the grade control prediction of what was sent to the mill.

evidence.note: Chip, muck and design grades as the production grade sources (er2022, er2016). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Compile reserve model grades for the mined shapes
steps.description: The geologist reports the reserve model tonnes and grade inside the month's mined development and stope shapes, so the grade control figures can be compared with the long-term model. Before 2021 this was the polygonal model; from 2021 the 3D block model.

evidence.note: Polygonal to 3D estimation change in 2021 (er2022); monthly comparison of production with the reserve model (island).

steps.name: Build the reconciliation workbook
steps.description: The engineer lines up planned, surveyed, hoisted and trucked, and milled tonnes, grade and ounces with the stockpile and broken-stock changes, and calculates the factors: grade control against the reserve model (F1), mill against grade control (F2) and mill against the model (F3).

error.defect_description: Formula or link error in the workbook.

evidence.note: F1, F2 and F3 reconciliation factors (parker).

steps.name: Review the mill-side numbers
steps.description: The metallurgist checks the weightometer calibration and moisture, compares the sampled head grade with the head back-calculated from gold produced and tailings, and accounts for gold locked up in the circuit at month end. Adjustments are written into the workbook with a note.

control.basis: Site metallurgical accounting procedure: weightometer calibration and head grade checks before month-end figures are used

evidence.note: Mill-side checks are standard metallurgical accounting practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check variances against tolerance
steps.description: The chief geologist looks at each stage-to-stage difference and the three factors and decides whether they are within the site's tolerance, about 5 to 10% on tonnes and ounces, or need investigating.

evidence.note: Global mine-to-mill reconciliation within 5% (er2022); 2019 Island Gold production 7% over model tonnes and 5% over ounces (island). Tolerance and share investigated are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Ask the mine captain to confirm tallies
steps.description: The chief geologist sends the captain the days and headings where tallies, survey and mill disagree, asking about missed loads, ore sent to waste fill or waste sent to the ore pass. The captain checks with the shift supervisors and answers on the next shift.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate the variance
steps.description: The chief geologist works through the likely causes: tally errors, misrouted loads, overbreak shown by cavity scans, chip sample bias, assay bias at the mine lab and broken stock. If the stockpile tonnes do not tie, the stockpiles are re-surveyed.

evidence.note: F2 points to unplanned dilution between ore control and mill (parker); chip bias and lab bias (er2022); overbreak root causes rarely backed by data (potvin).

steps.name: Drive to the stockpile pads
steps.description: A surveyor drives to the portal pad and the mill pad with the survey gear. In winter the survey waits for snow to be cleared or a whiteout to pass, since snow cover spoils the pile surface.

evidence.note: Portal pad and mill pad are 16.6 km apart (er2022 haul distance); weather delay is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Re-survey the stockpiles
steps.description: The surveyor picks up the toe and surface of each stockpile, builds a new surface and recalculates the volume and tonnes, then sends the figures to the chief geologist.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Correct the workbook and record explanations
steps.description: The engineer applies the confirmed tally corrections and revised stockpile tonnes, reruns the factors and writes a one-line explanation for each remaining variance.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Compare finished stopes with their designs
steps.description: For each stope finished in the month the engineer overlays the cavity scan on the design and calculates overbreak, underbreak and dilution against the 0.5 m hangingwall and footwall allowance, and the tonnes and grade recovered.

evidence.note: All benchmarked mines reconcile volume, tonnes and grade for each stope using CMS (potvin); 1.0 m overbreak measured at the reference mine (er2022).

steps.name: Write the reconciliation report
steps.description: The chief geologist writes the monthly report: the stage-by-stage table, the factors with year-to-date trends, stope dilution, the explained variances and actions for planning and grade control.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Technical services manager reviews the report
steps.description: The technical services manager reads the report, questions any explanation that does not hold up and sends it back for more work or accepts it.

control.basis: Technical services review of the monthly reconciliation before it feeds cost reporting and the qualified person's reserve update

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue the report
steps.description: The technical services manager emails the report to the planning engineers, the site controller for cost reporting and the resource geologist, and presents it at the monthly technical meeting.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the year-to-date reconciliation tracker
steps.description: The chief geologist adds the month to the year-to-date tracker of factors and stope dilution that feeds the year-end reserve update and the dilution assumptions in stope design.

evidence.note: Dilution factors in the reserve come from reconciling CMS data with stope designs (er2022); historical data used to forecast dilution (potvin).

exceptions.name: Variance outside tolerance
exceptions.description: Stage-to-stage differences exceed tolerance and are investigated with the captains.

exceptions.name: Stockpile re-survey
exceptions.description: Stockpile tonnes do not tie and the pads are re-surveyed, sometimes after waiting for weather.

exceptions.name: Report sent back
exceptions.description: The manager does not accept an explanation and asks for more investigation.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from met balance issued to reconciliation report issued

evidence.note: Author's estimate: met balance about day 3-5 after month end and report expected by about day 12-15 so it can feed the next plan.

benchmarks.unit: absolute difference, global mine production versus mill

evidence.note: Reported as within 5%.

benchmarks.unit: ratio of production reconciled to mill over reserve model

pain_points.description: Tonnes come from skip counts, truck counts, survey and the mill weightometer in separate spreadsheets, so errors only appear when the totals do not tie.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from the haulage chain in er2022.

pain_points.description: Shrink mucking leaves most broken ore in the stopes between months, so the month's mined tonnes rest on an estimate of broken stock.
Comparing cavity scans with designs means moving data between survey software, design software and spreadsheets.

evidence.note: Multiple software types make reconciliation time-consuming (potvin).

pain_points.description: Grade sources have known biases: chip samples run higher than core and the unaccredited mine lab showed bias on low-grade standards, which makes F1 and F2 hard to interpret.

assumptions: The case starts when the met balance is issued, a few days after month end; month-end survey pick-ups and the routine stockpile survey are done in their own processes and arrive as inputs.
Extra interfaces beyond the organisation file: the grade control model, the monthly plan and the hoist log as inputs.
The mine geologist, mine captain and surveyor take part, although the organisation file's process entry lists only the engineer, chief geologist, metallurgist and manager.
The surface pickup truck is not in the organisation file's resources; four is the author's estimate for technical services.
Ore is trucked 16.6 km from a portal pad to the mill (er2022), so there are two stockpiles to reconcile; the organisation file describes the mill as next to the shaft.
Steps s02-s04 and s06 run partly in parallel; their waits are kept short so the simulated cycle is not inflated.
Loaded costs per hour are taken from the organisation file.

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24 to match this workflow's sources: ids were renamed (mill-elution-refining to mill-gold-room-refining, loaded_carbon to gold_concentrate, tailings_slurry to filtered_tailings, elution-circuit to refinery), and roles and resources this workflow added are now in the organisation file. Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (CAPR001445)
sources.publisher: SRK Consulting (Canada) Inc. for Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd.
sources.supports: Reference mine practice: channel (chip) sampling of underground faces by production geologist and technician after each advance once the heading is inspected and supported, sample lengths 0.3 m minimum in ore and 0.3 m maximum with visible gold; test-hole, long-hole and muck sampling (one muck sample per 25-30 t truck, taken by muckers); samples brought to surface at end of the beat geologist's shift and shuttled daily to the company assay office in Wawa; mine lab not accredited, 11% QC insertion (blank, CRM, duplicate per 28-sample tray), VG protocol, low-grade CRM bias; channel results recorded in Promine; polygonal estimates before 2021, Leapfrog/Datamine 3D model from 2021; chip samples average higher than core; mine-to-mill reconciliation within 5%; stope design with 1.5 m minimum width, 0.5 m HW and FW dilution from CMS reconciliation, 90% stope and 99% development recovery, stope cut-off 5.5 g/t, development cut-off 2.0 g/t, density 2.7 t/m3; captive sub-level open stoping via Alimak raises, 13-18 m 64 mm down-holes on a 3-2-3 pattern, shrink mucking, CRF sill mats and URF fill; 19% of mill feed from sill development; ore hoisted in 4 t skips and trucked 16.6 km from the portal pad to the mill; two 12 h shifts 365 days a year; UG labour table with 9 mine engineering and 10 mine geology staff; recommendation to evaluate tools for short-term planning; ventilation rule 0.06 m3/s per kW of diesel

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Mining Complex including the Eagle River Gold Mine, the Mishi Gold Mine and Related Infrastructure
sources.publisher: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. (G. Mannard and P. Ng), hosted by minedocs.com
sources.supports: Chip samples taken every round (every 3 to 4 m) in ore development headings across the full face, about 2.5 kg, 0.3-0.5 m lengths; raises sometimes chip sampled and always muck sampled; muck sample per 25-30 t; sealed samples transported daily to the company Mine Assay office with results emailed to the mine; assay data in Microsoft Access linked to Promine and Surpac/Gemcom, databases updated weekly and audited monthly; about 30% of production from silling and development; CMS surveys show about 1.0 m wall overbreak; Mishi grade control on blast hole samples

sources.title: NI 43-101 Technical Report for the Island Gold Mine, Dubreuilville, Ontario, Canada (exhibit 99.1)
sources.publisher: Alamos Gold Inc. (filed on SEC EDGAR)
sources.supports: Neighbouring Wawa-area mine: resource shapes created by geology and passed to production engineering for mineable stope design with recovery and dilution factors; each stope gets a package with drilling plans, blast letters, ventilation and gas check instructions, mucking plans and backfilling directives; Matthews stability graph used for stope dimensions; CMS surveys and beat geologists control dilution while mucking; chip samples 1.5-2 kg taken by geological technician or geologist, assays entered into Promine; all underground production samples assayed at the Wesdome laboratory in Wawa; 2019 production reconciled to mill was 107% of tonnes, 98% of grade and 105% of ounces of the current reserve model, with monthly comparison going forward

sources.title: Benchmarking of stope design and reconciliation practices (Underground Mining Technology 2020)
sources.publisher: Australian Centre for Geomechanics (Y. Potvin, K.R. Woodward, B. McFadyen, I. Thin, D. Grant)
sources.supports: 2019 workshops in Perth and Rouyn-Noranda with 19 underground mines: stope design note contents (shape, wireframe, ground support, slot and rings, fill, ventilation, predicted overbreak); definition drilling completed ahead of design if needed; design about three months before extraction at large stopes and within a few weeks at small rapid-turnaround stopes; drill and blast design a few days before drilling; most mines have a comprehensive sign-off involving geotechnical, backfill, ventilation and management; stope reconciliation starts with CMS; all mines reconcile volume, tonnes and grade per stope and feed a periodic mine reconciliation led by geology; multiple software packages make reconciliation slow; narrow vein mines focus on hangingwall overbreak and ELOS

sources.title: Reconciliation principles for the mining industry (35th APCOM Symposium 2011), abstract
sources.supports: Reconciliation compares tonnes, grade and metal from exploration data, production sampling and plant data using factors: F1 grade control model versus reserves depleted, F2 mill received versus production delivered (unplanned dilution between ore control and mill), F3 overall; reconciliation should be part of the mining process and a key performance indicator
